scope.external_launch_access: Purchased Foreign Launch Partnership requires a real qualified human provider. Designated foreign-carriage programmes accept domestic OLV research OR a signed, trained and funded provider. Other mission architectures retain domestic launcher research.

roles.name: Scientific instruments
roles.work: Flight instruments, calibration, environmental testing and delivery to the operator.

roles.name: Tracking & communications
roles.work: Compatible tracking stations, radio links, scheduled coverage and telemetry handover.

roles.name: Mission operations
roles.work: Flight procedures, simulations, command interfaces and a joint operations team.

roles.name: Launch services
roles.work: Launch-vehicle integration, range coordination, interface qualification and launch support.
roles.hardware: Provider must hold real OLV research at the mission minimum and qualified orbital launch capabilities; crew transport additionally requires crewed-flight capability. National launcher development and qualification programmes cannot be outsourced.

agreement_process: Operator selects a current human country and work package in Mission Control / International operations.

Country must exist, be at peace with the operator, have the specified real national capabilities and researched payload or launcher hardware, have a free outbound order, and not already be an astronaut partner in the same mission.
Named recipient government accepts or declines a serial-bound 90-day invitation. An unresolved older popup cannot be overwritten.
Recipient finances mission-specific interface qualification weekly. Insufficient funds pause qualification without free progress. No universal refresher bypass is granted for different spacecraft.

Before departure, verify both governments are human, exact bindings and serials still match, prerequisites and technical capabilities remain valid, qualification is complete, and both treasuries cover the actual transaction. A generic external-access receipt is insufficient without domestic launcher research or a real signed provider. The purchased Foreign Launch Partnership specifically requires a real provider.

Freeze nationality, role, invoice and original mission probabilities at departure. Paid flight allocations cover the agreed delivery and support through mission completion; no additional running partner invoice or hidden RNG draw.
Issue country-specific partner outcome reports. Release only the matching work order. Keep joint completion in Records without awarding the operator's independent capabilities.

Outbound dashboard records each signed order independently, including its operator flag, mission, role, paid weeks, weekly appropriation, flight allocation and procurement invoice. Role-specific outcome events retain native FROM/ROOT country scopes when two reports arrive together.

financial_model.scientific_tracking_operations: Partner finances 10% of the existing mission bill at departure; host pays the remaining 90%, before separate crew contributions. Preparation is additional paid work.
financial_model.launch_services: Provider finances the 30% manufacturing/integration share of the existing mission bill. Host pays the provider a 35% procurement invoice, and the existing national mission bill is reduced by the replaced 30% share. Net host mission charge is 105%, provider receives a net 5% before its preparation costs. No second charge for the same hardware.
financial_model.rounding: Transfers are rounded down to whole millions before guards and runtime charging. Displayed totals are previews; the native launch guard checks exact signed contracts.
financial_model.funding_units: MD billions; all recurring charges are weekly.
financial_model.balance: Shares, invoices, weeks and costs are campaign balance, not claims about historical contracts.

awards.maximum_combined_example: Two astronaut countries and one operational partner: operator 50%, astronaut countries 20% each, operational partner 10%.
awards.research: First qualifying programme: original 10% one-use general research award split by share; first achievement: original 20% split likewise. One use for any technology per recipient.
awards.repeat: No repeat science, political power or general research. Capped repeat prestige is shared from the existing pool. First/partial guest receipts are shared with the astronaut route to prevent duplicate first-success claims by changing roles.
awards.world_first: Operator remains the registered first-country holder. Frozen operational contributor and role appear in international news.
awards.ai_takeover: Frozen signed award entitlement is escrowed until human control returns; no active AI programme or payout.
awards.casualties: Ground and instrument personnel are not aboard. Only astronaut manifests can incur astronaut manpower loss.
awards.hardware_chance: For eligible foreign-carriage missions, the actual contracted provider OLV generation supplies the capped launcher-generation probability component. No OLV research is transferred to the client.

historical_precedents.evidence: NASA supplied the spacecraft, telescope, spectrographs and one observatory; ESA supplied solar panels and the second observatory; the United Kingdom supplied detector and sensor hardware. Scientific operations were performed through ground observatories.
historical_precedents.design_use: Separate instrument, tracking and operations responsibilities; participation without a national crewed vehicle.

historical_precedents.evidence: Europe funded, designed and built the laboratory and delivered engineering and first flight units plus ground equipment in exchange for a shared first mission; first-mission payload allocation was shared.
historical_precedents.design_use: Funded deliverables, integration and formal acceptance in exchange for shared scientific credit, while the launch operator retains flight authority.

historical_precedents.programme: Symphonie, French-German cooperation and purchased US launches, 1974-1975
historical_precedents.evidence: Bilateral project teams and industrial integration preceded Thor-Delta launches following Europa II difficulties.
historical_precedents.design_use: Distinguish scientific co-development from procured launch services; an actual service provider has technical responsibilities and an invoice.

assets.share_bar: Original crew chrome expanded to six conserved-share frames, 100/90/80/70/60/50.
assets.native_flags: Existing current-country GetFlag masked shields; upstream MD/base-game credits and separate redistribution permission remain unknown, as recorded in crew-ui-notice.json.
assets.events: Existing mission-control illustration and native MD event-frame assets reused unchanged; original credits and permissions remain in existing news/event-art notices.
assets.licence: No new third-party material copied by this extension. Licence for standalone redistribution of inherited native assets remains unknown.
assets.original_chrome_credit: Generated during the authorized IMPERIA COLD WAR coding session; project distribution licence unspecified. The user authorized in-game creation and integration.

save_compatibility: New variables default to no operational partner. Existing flights receive no retrospective country, cost, award split or probability change. Existing astronaut variables and saved national capability receipts are retained. Legacy generic external-access capabilities remain as earned programme knowledge, but alone do not authorize a new foreign-carriage departure.
remaining_abstractions: Launch services verify the supplier country, qualification, research and paid integration; physical state-based launchpads, hardware inventory and pad queues remain outside this module.

The legacy Interkosmos research-cosmonaut programme still uses its original contracted foreign pilot rather than the new astronaut nationality roster. Its launch carrier must now be a named provider unless the client meets domestic launcher research.
One operational package per mission is deliberate. Several provider work packages on a single spacecraft and long-term station logistics are not implemented.
Flight-support allocations are prepaid and contractual; individual ground-station schedules, staff inventories and staged acceptance reviews are not simulated.

verification.preview_type: Offline native GUI/GFX/font composition, not an in-game screenshot.
verification.native_ui_variants: Signed mission work-package view plus a separate country dashboard when the selected programme has no transferable flight package.
